items.title: Expected query cost from finite execution prefixes
items.statement_or_definition: A sequential procedure has finite outcome sets and a specified normalized transition law at each elementary step. Its first M elementary steps give a finite experiment; let C_M be the number of oracle calls executed by that prefix, with a halted branch extended by deterministic idle steps. Define expected query cost as sup_M E[C_M] in [0,∞]. Define total query count pathwise as sup_M C_M; an infinite execution can have finite query count. No finite-prefix experiment is claimed to determine min(total queries,M) when arbitrarily many nonquery steps intervene.
proof_obligations: Prove prefix consistency by summing the last transition law, C_M≤C_(M+1) pathwise, and finite-prefix expectation monotonicity. For a procedure whose round contains a bounded finite number of nonquery steps, define finite first-R-round experiments and compute their query expectations; cofinal prefix/round limits give the same supremum. In Simon, one query occurs per sampling round, so query-index truncations are valid specifically there.

items.title: Gaussian elimination over F2 for Simon recovery
items.statement_or_definition: Input a binary d×n matrix, d=n−1, n≥1. Set pivot row k=0. For columns j=0,…,n−1 find the least row i≥k with entry 1; if none, continue to next column. items.title: Classical randomized Simon search needs exponential queries
items.statement_or_definition: Let N=2^n and n≥8. Any worst-case randomized algorithm that outputs the hidden nonzero s with success at least 2/3 requires Ω(2^{n/2}) classical oracle queries. For q distinct queried addresses, put B=binom(q,2) and S=N−1. Under a collision-free adaptive transcript, the posterior is uniform over at least S−B masks. At the jth new query, at most j−1 remaining masks create a collision with a prior address, so the total collision probability is at most B/(S−B). The no-collision transcript permits guessing success at most 1/(S−B), giving average success at most (B+1)/(S−B). In particular, if q≤floor(2^{n/2}/4), then B≤N/32 and this success bound is <2/3. Averaging the same bound over random coins proves the randomized lower bound.
proof_obligations: Prove uniformity of the posterior after each collision-free adaptive transcript because distinct coset labels are assigned uniformly without replacement; at each fresh query count at most j−1 colliding masks among at least S−binom(j−1,2) candidates; sum these conditional bounds to B/(S−B), then bound the no-collision guess probability by 1/(S−B). Apply the fixed cutoff q≤floor(2^{n/2}/4), n≥8, and average over random coins. Separate oracle queries from classical bit cost.

items.title: Finite universal-gate compilation cost for the truncated QFT
items.statement_or_definition: For n≥1 and rational target error 0<η<1, let m=min(n,ceil(log₂(4πn/η))) and compile the truncated circuit with this cutoff. The omitted rotations contribute operator error at most η/2 (or zero if m=n). Let L=O(nm) count the Hadamard and controlled-phase blocks, with final swaps expanded into exact CNOTs. Under QC12’s fixed-arity QSD, exact-CNOT, inverse-closed dense one-qubit alphabet and exact-arithmetic compiler hypotheses, set δ=min(η/(2L), ε₀/2), where ε₀ is the fixed compiler threshold, and compile each one-qubit block and each complete controlled-phase block to projective operator error at most δ. Do not control a phase-minimized subblock. Projective errors telescope to at most η/2 for the truncated circuit and at most η from the exact QFT. The projective-distance output theorem gives total-variation error at most η for every computational-basis output law. The finite gate count is O(nm·log^{3.97}(2nm/η)) including O(nm) exact CNOTs from fixed-arity decompositions and O(n) swap CNOTs. Per-block scalar phases are retained as QC12 metadata: they are harmless for this standalone output law and become relative under outer control, for which this theorem claims no compilation cost. This is an abstract gate-count result under QC12’s exact-arithmetic compiler interface, with no finite-precision target-angle bit-time claim.
proof_obligations: For m=min(n,ceil(log₂(4πn/η))), apply the truncation theorem: the operator error is at most η/2, or zero when m=n.

Let L count the H and complete controlled-phase blocks (L=O(nm)); expand each final SWAP into three exact CNOTs. Since δ=min(η/(2L), ε₀/2) is within the fixed QC12 compiler range, apply its full-block projective corollary to every one- or two-qubit block, compiling each controlled phase as the complete CPθ target and never as a controlled phase-minimized subblock.

Use the triangle inequality for projective operator distance to combine the L gate errors into at most Lδ≤η/2, and combine with the truncation error to obtain projective distance at most η from the exact QFT. Apply thm-qa-projective-operator-closeness-bounds-output-distribution separately to truncation and compilation and use total-variation triangle inequality to obtain η/2+η/2=η.

Track the product of per-block scalar metadata as one whole-circuit scalar; use standalone global-phase invariance for this output law. Do not claim that the scalar can be discarded under outer control or that an outer-controlled QFT is compiled. The cost is O(L·log^{3.97}(1/δ)) one-qubit gates plus exact CNOT terms, hence O(nm·log^{3.97}(2nm/η)) including exact CNOTs; make no finite-precision target-angle bit-time claim.
